_note: Plain-English translation of token budgets per AI plan. Used by `forge profile show` to make limits meaningful to non-engineers. Update when AI providers change their plans. Source: Anthropic / Cursor / OpenAI public pricing pages, refreshed quarterly.
_methodology: Token caps for consumer plans (Claude Pro/Max, Cursor Pro/Business, Codex CLI) are not officially published as numeric per-session limits -- providers use rolling-window or 'fair use' models. Numbers here are empirical estimates from factory_metrics.jsonl observed burn rates (marked `empirical: true`). API plans (api-direct) and BYOK use pay-per-token billing with no per-session cap from the provider; we use sensible factory-side defaults.

claude-free.what_you_get: ~30 messages per 5-hour window on Claude.ai, very limited Claude Code access
claude-free.good_for: trying it out, single-file tweaks, learning
claude-free.not_for: multi-file refactors, big projects, daily work
claude-free.empirical_note: 5-hour rolling window not published as exact tokens; estimate from factory_metrics.jsonl 2026-05 burn

claude-pro.what_you_get: ~5x the Free tier; Claude Code with reasonable limits
claude-pro.good_for: solo dev work, multiple projects, side projects
claude-pro.not_for: agency multi-client work, large monorepos, all-day coding
claude-pro.empirical_note: Claude Pro 'roughly 5x Free' is Anthropic's public language; exact per-session token cap not published

claude-max.what_you_get: 5x or 20x the Pro tier; for serious daily use
claude-max.good_for: production work, daily coding, complex projects
claude-max.empirical_note: Max is sold as 5x/20x Pro; daily token figure assumes the 20x Max tier observed in heavy use

cursor-free.empirical_note: Cursor advertises completions + slow premium requests, not tokens; conversion estimated

cursor-pro.not_for: very heavy daily use beyond ~500 premium requests
cursor-pro.empirical_note: Token figure derived from 500 fast premium requests/mo at typical ~7k tokens/request

cursor-business.what_you_get: Pro + team management, SSO, privacy mode
cursor-business.empirical_note: Business tier inherits Pro request budgets plus team admin features; tokens estimated

codex-free.what_you_get: OpenAI free credits ($5 trial), gpt-4o-mini access
codex-free.empirical_note: OpenAI free tier is credit-based ($5 trial); token figure assumes gpt-4o-mini at ~$0.15/1M input

codex-paid.what_you_get: Pay per token used + gpt-4o / o1 access
codex-paid.limit_resets: no monthly limit; billed per use
codex-paid.good_for: predictable usage costs; large monthly volumes
codex-paid.not_for: users who want a fixed cap
codex-paid.empirical_note: Pay-as-you-go has no fixed monthly cap; figure is typical agent-coding usage at $20/mo ChatGPT Plus equivalent

api-direct.what_you_get: No hard limit; you set budget alerts
api-direct.good_for: agencies, production AI features, BYOK customers
api-direct.not_for: users who want a fixed monthly cap
api-direct.empirical_note: API plans have no per-session cap; numbers are sensible factory-side defaults for warning thresholds

byok.what_you_get: Each tenant supplies their own API key; you bill them separately
byok.not_for: solo devs (BYOK overhead not worth it)
byok.empirical_note: Per-tenant; whatever the tenant's API key allows. Factory tracks aggregate but doesn't gate per-tenant

_translations_help._note: How to translate token counts into human terms in `forge profile show` output

examples.50000: about 20-50 back-and-forth messages, or one focused 30-min task
examples.150000: about 60-150 messages, or one full afternoon of coding
examples.300000: about 100-300 messages, multiple sessions per day

rules_of_thumb: 1000 tokens is roughly 750 words OR 50 lines of code
An average message exchange uses 2000-5000 tokens incl. context
Running a subagent costs 10000-30000 tokens for a typical task
